takeaway: Gilbert's syndrome: a common hereditary cause of mild intermittent jaundice with unconjugated hyperbilirubinaemia and otherwise normal liver tests.

question.text: A 25-year-old man has had mild intermittent jaundice for 6 years. Blood tests show moderate unconjugated hyperbilirubinaemia, with normal liver function tests and histology. Likely diagnosis?
question.say: A twenty-five-year-old man has noticed mild intermittent jaundice for the past six years. His blood tests show a moderate unconjugated hyperbilirubinaemia, with otherwise normal liver function tests and normal hepatic histology. What is the likely diagnosis?

lines.text: A 25-year-old man with mild, intermittent jaundice for 6 years.
lines.say: This twenty-five-year-old man has had mild, intermittent jaundice for six years. A gentle yellow glow.
His blood shows a moderate rise in unconjugated bilirubin.

lines.text: But the liver tests are normal.
lines.say: (laugh) But the liver is smiling, because the liver function tests and the histology are normal.

lines.text: Fasting can bring the jaundice on.
lines.say: Mild jaundice may appear with fasting and exertion.
It may also appear with stress and infections.

lines.text: It is a common hereditary condition, autosomal dominant.
lines.say: Gilbert's syndrome is a common hereditary cause of unconjugated bilirubin, with an autosomal dominant pattern.

lines.text: Remember: mild intermittent jaundice with normal liver tests is Gilbert's syndrome.
lines.say: Remember: mild intermittent jaundice with normal liver tests is Gilbert's syndrome.
